example.message: Token (kid=frontend) is not authorized for scope=settle

Forbidden.description: Token authenticated but lacks the endpoint's scope (XL-4)

NotFound.description: Intent / quote not found or expired

example.message: Too many requests. Please try again later.

RateLimited.description: Per-IP or per-user rate limit exceeded (L-2)

example.message: HTTPS is required. If you are behind a TLS-terminating proxy, ensure it sets x-forwarded-proto: https.

TlsRequired.description: Request reached the listener over plain HTTP (XL-3)

Unauthorized.description: Missing or invalid bearer token / X-API-Key

BigIntString.description: Positive integer as string (token amounts in base units).

address_format.description: Address format used by this chain. "hex20" for EVM (0x-prefixed 40-char hex), "base58check" for Tron, "base58" for Solana.

min_stealth_notional_usd.description: Minimum order notional (USD) for a solvable stealth/shielded quote settling on this chain: destination fill + sponsored ERC-4337 claim cost, times the gas-floor margin. A consumer may pre-decline a stealth order below this before quoting. Null when the gas oracle cannot price the chain, or for non-EVM chains (no 4337 claim leg). L1 destinations are materially higher than L2s.

vm_type.description: VM type for address format selection.

corridors.description:
Mover-backed corridors with per-corridor bounds, reflecting the real
mover config: CCTP for USDC across the EVM chains, RelayMover for the
USDT corridors, RelayDrain for the USDG exit.

**Not the routability gate.** This list covers the EVM movers only; a
deposit-address route (a Tron leg, in either direction) is quotable
and fills without ever appearing here. Treating an absent pair as
unsupported therefore pre-declines routes the solver serves. The
authority for what is routable is `chains` plus
`tokens[].pull_methods`; use `corridors` for per-corridor bounds and
mover attribution. Absent/empty is a valid degrade.

cross_chain_only.description:
When true, origin and destination chains must differ. When false,
a same-chain route is additionally fillable for a PUBLIC
settlement of an advertised `conversion_pairs` entry that carries
`strategy: float` and `same_chain: true`, on an EVM chain both
its tokens sit on. It reads false only while such an entry exists
(XOCHI_SAME_CHAIN_FILLS on AND the row opted in), never merely
because the switch is on. Same-token same-chain is never fillable;
every other same-chain request is refused with
`same_chain_unsupported`, whose message names the failing rule.

deposit_attestation_signer.description:
Lowercased 0x address of the key that signs deposit-route
`deposit_attestation`s. The client pins this and rejects any quote
whose attestation does not recover to it. Null when no HD wallet
secret is configured. Distinct from the solver collection address.

deposit_attestation_vectors_sha256.description:
Lowercase SHA-256 hex of the exact bytes served at
`deposit_attestation_vectors_url`, so a client can detect drift
without downloading them. The served ETag is its first 16 characters.

deposit_attestation_vectors_url.description:
Path serving the conformance vectors for that version. Consume these
rather than keeping a local copy; a copy cannot detect its own
staleness.

deposit_attestation_version.description:
The attestation message-format version this server SIGNS, read from
the server's own constant. Compare it against your pinned constant
to name a version skew directly: without this field a skew is
indistinguishable from an outage, because a client verifying the
wrong field set fails closed and reports only that the signature did
not recover to the pinned signer.

pull_deadline_buffer_seconds.description:
Seconds by which the on-chain pull authorization (ERC-3009
`valid_before` / Permit2 `deadline`) outlives the signed
`XochiIntent.deadline`, which is the quote's `expires_at`.

Operator-tunable, so a client bounding a pull's expiry would
otherwise have to guess a ceiling. This window is the only place
on-chain authority outlives the deal the user signed.

erc3009.description: The ERC-3009 `to` a pull on this chain will name.

permit2.description: The Permit2 `spender` a pull on this chain will name.

pull_recipients.description:
Who receives an origin pull, keyed by chain id then pull method. The
client SHOULD pin these and reject a quote whose
`pull_authorization` names a different recipient.

This is the one field of a pull authorization the client cannot
derive: `to` (ERC-3009) and `spender` (Permit2) depend on which
chains have the verified pull proxy enabled, which is deployment
config the client has no view of. Any client-side expectation would
be either wrong (rejecting honest quotes the moment a chain enables
the proxy) or vacuous. It is also the field that moves the money.

The two methods vary independently -- they are separate deployments
behind separate flags -- so a chain may show a proxy for one and the
solver EOA for the other.

EVM chains only. A chain is ABSENT rather than null when no
recipient resolves; there is then no expectation to pin, which is
distinct from "any address is acceptable". Non-EVM origins have no
signed pull at all -- they use `deposit_address` +
`deposit_attestation`.

Advisory over the same channel as the quote, like
`deposit_attestation_signer`: it closes tampering in transit or a
compromised quote path, and lets a taker pin the values out of band.
It is not a defence against an attacker controlling the channel end
to end.

spec_version.description:
SemVer of the `@riddler/spec` document this server conforms to.
Lets a taker gate on the normative layered fee model (SPEC section
4) rather than inferring support from a quote's shape. MAJOR
signals a breaking wire or signature-construction change.

stealth_factory_address.description:
Canonical SimpleAccount factory that owns stealth counterfactual
accounts. Lets the client verify a recovered stealth signer via
`getAddress(owner, 0)` without pinning the address itself.

ChainAddress.description:
Address in any supported chain format. EVM chains use a 0x-prefixed
40-char hex string; TVM (Tron) and SVM (Solana) chains use a base58
string of 32–44 characters.

ChainId.description:
1=Ethereum, 10=Optimism, 100=Gnosis, 137=Polygon, 4663=Robinhood Chain,
5042=Arc, 8453=Base, 42161=Arbitrum, 84532=Base Sepolia,
421614=Arbitrum Sepolia, 11155111=Sepolia,
11155420=Optimism Sepolia, 728126428=Tron.

This enum is every chain the server can advertise, NOT every chain a
given deploy serves. Flag-gated chains (Arc behind `ENABLE_ARC`, Gnosis
behind `ENABLE_GNOSIS`, Tron behind `ENABLE_TRON`) are absent from
`GET /xochi/chains` until their flag is on, and a quote naming one is
rejected `unsupported_chain`.
Read `/xochi/chains` for what this deploy actually serves.

Testnet IDs (84532, 11155111, 421614, 11155420) are enabled by
`TESTNET_ONLY=true`.

ClaimPrepareMultiRequest.description: Multi-account prepare (#1116). The action and the inner call(s) apply to every named account -- one decision over a set is the point -- but the PROOFS are per account, because each stealth account has its own owner key and no single signature could speak for the set. An account whose proof is missing or wrong is refused on its own and the rest still prepare; when every account is refused, one refusal is returned with the same code the single-account form would have given -- the first TRANSIENT one if any (#853), else the first.

counterfactual_addresses.description: The counterfactuals to prepare, each scanned from its own ERC-5564 announcement. No repeats: preparing one account twice would charge its rate-limit bucket twice and hand back two ops to choose between. Bounded because each account costs a sponsorship and an RPC probe, which the per-counterfactual limiter cannot see the width of.

proofs.description: One proof per account, each over that account's own challenge. Matched by `counterfactual_address`, never positionally: a client that reorders its accounts must not hand one account's proof to another and read the refusal as its own bug.

ops.description: One prepared op per account that passed, in the order named. Sign each `userOpHash` with that account's own stealth key.

refused.description: The accounts that were not prepared, each with its own reason. A refusal here is per account: the others were prepared and can be submitted. An account whose ownership proof is absent, wrong or replayed answers `not_found` -- identical to an unknown counterfactual, so a 20-wide request cannot classify scanned announcements into "holds funds" / "already swept" / "not ours" (#993). A STALE proof answers `ownership_proof_stale`, as on the single form: signer recovery runs first, so only the key holder can ever see it, and it re-signs with a current timestamp.

ClaimPrepareProofVectors.description:
Conformance vectors for the `/xochi/claim/prepare` ownership-proof
challenge (#993). Riddler is authoritative for this set: it verifies
the proof, so the challenge encoding it accepts is the contract a
signer must match byte-for-byte.

challenge_version.description: The challenge prefix these vectors cover.

signer.description:
The stealth address the vectors' signatures recover to -- a
well-known published test key, never a production key. In a real
claim the signer is the intent's stealth address.

vectors.description: One case per encoding rule the challenge must not get wrong.

challenge.description: The exact UTF-8 challenge string signed.

inputs.description: The request fields the challenge is built from. chain_id is the CLAIM (destination) chain.

private_key.description: The well-known test key that signed this vector.

signer.description: The address the signature recovers to.

action.description: What the prepared op does (#1103). `transfer` (default): the original sweep, `execute(to_token, 0, transfer(recipient_address, to_amount))`; a successful submit marks the intent completed. `approve_permit2`: `execute(to_token, 0, approve(PERMIT2, to_amount))` -- the account grants Permit2 an allowance over its full balance so it can be the ORIGIN of a Xochi intent (the stealth owner signs the pull via ERC-1271); funds stay in place and the intent stays claimable. `call` (#1115): an arbitrary inner call from the account, admitted only if `{target, selector}` and every argument word satisfy this deploy's allowlist (see /xochi/vectors/claim-actions.json); terminality and the gas ceiling come from the matching row. Non-transfer actions ALWAYS require the ownership proof, signed over the v2 challenge `xochi-claim-prepare-v2:{chain_id}:{counterfactual}:{action}:{recipient}:{issued_at}` -- or, for `call`, the v3 challenge `xochi-claim-prepare-v3:{chain_id}:{counterfactual}:call:{call_hash}:{recipient}:{issued_at}` where `call_hash` is keccak256(target(20) || selector(4) || args || value(32)) over raw bytes, so a captured proof cannot be reused for a different call (see /xochi/vectors/claim-prepare-proof.json). Amounts are never taken from the request.

args.description: ABI-encoded argument words for the inner call: whole 32-byte words only, and exactly as many as the allowlist row declares. Dynamic tails (bytes, arrays) are not accepted -- an argument this server cannot decode is one it cannot police. An amount word is bounded by the intent's to_amount; an address word must satisfy the row's policy.

calls.description: The call list for `action: batch` (#1116), executed as one `executeBatch` op: one signature, one sponsorship, and the calls land atomically -- an approve and the pull that consumes it are never separated by a window in which the allowance sits granted with nothing to spend it. Every entry is resolved through the same allowlist as a single `call`, so a batch can reach nothing a `call` could not, and one refused entry refuses the WHOLE batch (422, naming the entry's index). The sponsored-gas ceiling is the sum of the matched rows' ceilings, and the batch is terminal if any entry is.

counterfactual_address.description: The counterfactual SimpleAccount address the recipient scanned from the ERC-5564 announcement. The server resolves the intent from it; the client never sends intent_id.

ownership_proof.description: Stealth-key proof of control (#993): 65-byte r||s||v signature over keccak256 of the claim-prepare challenge (see the endpoint description for the exact string). Must be sent TOGETHER with proof_issued_at -- either both or neither; a half-pair is refused 422. Required once XOCHI_CLAIM_PROOF_REQUIRED is on; always verified when present. Single-use -- re-sign with a fresh proof_issued_at for every prepare.

proof_issued_at.description: Unix seconds baked into the signed challenge. Accepted from 300s in the past to 30s in the future of server time. Must be sent TOGETHER with ownership_proof -- either both or neither; a half-pair is refused 422.

selector.description: The 4-byte function selector of the inner call. Required with `action: call`.

target.description: The contract the account calls. Required with `action: call`, refused with any other action (a silently ignored target reads as though it were honoured). Not allowlisted -> 422.

value.description: Native wei sent with the inner call. Must be "0": stealth settlement is ERC-20 end to end until #1102.

action.description: The action this op performs, echoed from the request (#1103). Decode callData accordingly: `transfer` wraps `transfer(recipient, amount)`, `approve_permit2` wraps `approve(PERMIT2, amount)`. A deployed counterfactual is served with `factory` null and `factoryData` "0x"; an undeployed one carries the SimpleAccountFactory initCode.

counterfactualAddress.description: SimpleAccount holding the settled funds; the op sender.

entryPoint.description: EntryPoint v0.8 address folded into the EIP-712 domain separator userOpHash was computed over. Required to recompute the digest.

stealthAddress.description: Stealth-derived owner of the counterfactual account.

userOpHash.description: EIP-712 digest of userOperation over entryPoint and chainId. Signed raw (no EIP-191 prefix), as EntryPoint v0.8 SimpleAccount expects. Do not sign this without first deriving it from userOperation -- see the userOperation description.

userOperation.description: The sponsored, unsigned UserOperation, in ERC-4337 JSON-RPC form (hex-quantity strings; paymaster and factory may be null). Served so the client can recompute userOpHash itself and decode callData to confirm the transfer targets the recipient it asked for, rather than signing an opaque digest on the venue's word (#847). A signature over a bare digest is valid for any preimage hashing to it, so a client that skips this check cannot detect a substituted op.

ClaimRebuildRequest.description: Deliberately has no field for the payout token or amount. `/claim/prepare` passes both straight into the ERC-20 transfer it builds, so a caller able to name them could name their own payout; they are read from the announcement metadata instead.

announcement_tx_hash.description: Transaction that emitted the ERC-5564 `Announcement`. Read by hash rather than scanned: these records are months old, and eth_getLogs is range-bounded. A hash pointing at an announcement this solver did not make matches nothing.

chain_id.description: Chain the announcement was emitted on.

counterfactual_address.description: The counterfactual SimpleAccount address holding the funds, as scanned from the ERC-5564 announcement.

owner_address.description: The stealth owner EOA the recipient derived from its viewing key. Verified against the announced counterfactual under CREATE2 -- a wrong owner is refused with `owner_mismatch` and nothing is written.

rebuilt.description: true when this call wrote the record; false when a claimable record was already present and nothing was written.

ClaimRefusal.description: One entry's refusal inside a 200 multi response. `code` is the same `ErrorCode` the single-account form would have answered with, so a client has one table for both shapes; `retryAfter` is present exactly when the refusal is transient (#853); `reason` is present when several refusals share a code, so a budget skip (`fan_out_deadline`, retry now) is told from a running orphan (`fan_out_overran`, wait `retryAfter`) or a sponsor outage without parsing `message`.

reason.description: Machine-readable sub-reason where `code` alone is ambiguous: the same `details.reason` the single form carries (`fan_out_deadline`, `fan_out_overran`, `fan_out_unavailable`, `sponsor_unavailable`, `receipt_pending`, ...).

retryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before retrying this entry. Transient refusals only.

userOpHash.description: Present on `/claim/submit` refusals; the hash the caller sent.

signatures.description: One {user_op_hash, signature} per prepared op (#1116). Entries are all parsed before any is submitted -- a malformed entry is a bug about the whole request, and spending the well-formed prefix first would burn signatures the caller is about to resend. Submission itself is per op: there is no batching at the bundler, so one bad signature fails alone. Bounded by the same number as `counterfactual_addresses`, because it is the same claim-all: every entry is a bundler submission plus a receipt poll, and the batch shares one budget (`XOCHI_CLAIM_FAN_OUT_BUDGET_MS`, 8 seconds by default). A non-object entry is a 422 naming its index.

pending.description: Ops the bundler accepted whose receipt was not seen inside this request's share of the budget. Not failures: each is in the mempool and will execute. Resubmit its `userOpHash` after `retryAfter` to poll it -- the op is never resent.

ClaimSubmitMultiResult.description: One `submitted` entry of the multi form: a `ClaimSubmitResult` keyed by the `userOpHash` the caller sent, so a partly-successful claim-all can be reconciled against the ops it signed. The single form carries no `userOpHash`.

opHash.description: The UserOperation hash the bundler returned for the accepted op.

retryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before resubmitting this entry to poll it.

user_op_hash.description: The userOpHash returned by /claim/prepare. The server looks the prepared op up by this hash and reads the bound intent from it, so the client sends no intent_id; a concurrent prepare for the same account cannot redirect this signature onto a different op.

ClaimSubmitResult.description: What a client-signed submit returns once the op's receipt is seen.

CompressedSecp256k1PubKey.description:
Compressed secp256k1 public key (33 bytes). Prefix `02` or `03`
followed by the 32-byte X coordinate.

mover.description: The mover that fills this corridor (observability only).

DepositAttestationVectors.description:
Conformance vectors for the deposit attestation, generated by this
server. Riddler is authoritative for this set: it signs the message and
the client only verifies it, so the expectation must come from the
producer.

signer.description:
The address that signed THESE VECTORS -- derived from the public
all-`abandon` BIP-39 test mnemonic, not from this deploy's key. Do
NOT pin it: the production signer is `deposit_attestation_signer` on
`/xochi/capabilities`, and pinning the value here would reject every
legitimate quote.

vectors.description: One case per encoding rule the format must not get wrong.

version.description: The message-format version these vectors cover. Equals `deposit_attestation_version` on `/xochi/capabilities`.

changedAt.description: Unix timestamp (seconds) of the authoritative mutation.

ErrorCode.description: Stable machine-readable error code (#692). The full client-facing catalog for /xochi/*; codes are append-only and never repurposed. 4xx codes are client-actionable (fix the request / re-quote); 503 codes are transient (retry shortly); 500 `internal_error` is on us.

details.description: Structured, machine-readable context for the rejection. Notable keys by code: `min_order_usd` (amount_below_minimum), `max_order_usd` (amount_above_maximum), `min_fillable_usd` (unprofitable), `supported_chains` (unsupported_chain), `available` (settlement_not_allowed), `retry_after` (rate_limit_exceeded, pre_positioning), `token` (insufficient_liquidity, pre_positioning), `reason` + `scope` (insufficient_liquidity: `reason` is absent for a genuine shortfall, `inventory_unverified` when the float cannot be read, `float_committed` when, at /execute, a deposit that landed since the quote committed the float it was admitted against -- the quote stays executable, retry shortly or requote -- or `quote_holds_exhausted` when unexecuted quotes hold it -- then `scope` is `caller` for the credential's own cap or `recipient` for the per-recipient sub-cap), `oracle` + `chain_id` (gas_price_unavailable), field-keyed message arrays (validation_failed).

message.description: Human-readable, user-safe description. Vetted to contain no internal hostnames, stack traces, raw revert data, or infra identifiers -- safe to surface to end users as-is. Map `error` codes to your own UX copy where you need tighter control; `message` prose may be refined without notice, codes are stable. For `validation_failed` the message names the offending fields (`Request validation failed: recipient_address, wallet`) so a proxy that forwards only `error` and `message` still carries a diagnosable reason; the per-field reasons remain in `details`.

nonce.description:
Ignored. The signed struct no longer carries a nonce (replay is
guarded by `intent_id`); accepted for backward compatibility only.

pull_signature.description:
Signature over the quote's `pull_authorization` typed data
(ERC-3009 / Permit2, per `payment_method`). Required in practice:
Riddler pulls `from_amount` on the origin chain before settling the
destination, so /execute fails closed with 400 (`pull_signature is
required ...`) when it is missing or invalid.

signature.description: EIP-712 signature from the quote's `eip712` typed data.

IntentLifecycleStatus.description:
Intent lifecycle. Terminal states are `completed`, `refunded`, `failed`,
`expired`. `refund_pending` means a refund is durably queued but not yet
confirmed on-chain; clients must keep polling until `refunded` carries a
real `refundTxHash`. `pull_pending` is a non-terminal state emitted only
when the server runs `/execute` asynchronously (returns 202): the origin
pull is broadcast and the destination fill follows once its receipt
confirms.
Mirrored from `Riddler.Integrations.Xochi.Schemas.IntentStatus`.

IntentStatus.description:
camelCase wire format (matches Xochi frontend / agent SDK
conventions). Optional fields are present only when relevant to the
intent's settlement type.

lifecycle.description: Versioned authoritative lifecycle for deposit-address routes. Acceptance closure and fund disposition are independent; consumers apply only snapshots whose revision is greater than the last applied revision. Absent on non-deposit and pre-contract intents.

receivingTxHash.description: Recipient stealth sweep (the counterfactual SimpleAccount -> the recipient's address), present only after a claim. This is NOT the settlement receipt -- use settlementTxHash for the fill receipt CTA.

settlementChainId.description: Chain the settlement receipt (settlementTxHash) lives on. For a stealth L1 settle this is Ethereum mainnet (1), not the origin chain, so key the explorer link off this rather than fromChainId. Falls back to the intent destination chain for legacy entries.

settlementConfirmed.description: True once Riddler has executed and recorded the settlement. Xochi may treat this as equivalent to a delivered settlement-ready webhook -- use it to reconcile an intent whose webhook was missed (a false value only means the settle has not completed yet). Always present.

settlementTxHash.description: On-chain settlement/fill receipt: solver -> recipient for a public fill, solver -> stealth address for a stealth fill. Already public on-chain, and the primary receipt CTA -- key the "view receipt" link and the exit from the "Settling" state off this field. Present once the fill lands. Distinct from receivingTxHash.

LayeredFeeBreakdown.description:
Itemized fee anatomy (economics.md Part 1). Three additive bps layers on a
never-discounted cost floor: solver spread + gas floor (Riddler), venue
(Xochi), routing (Raxol -> buyback), plus size-dependent price impact.
Discounts carve venue + routing only; the solver spread is identical at every
tier. Amounts are in destination-token smallest units (may be "0", so plain
strings rather than BigIntString); rates are in bps.

gas_floor.description:
Dynamic gas-floor top-up = total_fee minus the bps layers: "0" on
normal orders, the floor delta (live cost-to-fill x a safety margin,
minus the bps layers) on low-value orders where the percentage fee
falls below the cost to fill. Guarantees solver_fee + price_impact +
venue_fee + routing_fee + gas_floor.amount == total_fee. The route-real
gas estimate is the separate `estimated_gas_cost` (wei).

price_impact_bps.description: >0 only on large-vs-depth fills; render as a warning.

routing_fee_bps.description: Raxol routing fee, in bps. Discounted by tier; funds buyback.

solver_fee_bps.description: Riddler spread, in bps. Never discounted (the floor).

surplus_share_pct.description: 15 -- solver upside on positive slippage; user keeps 85%.

venue_fee_bps.description: Xochi venue fee, in bps. Discounted by tier.

expires_at.description: Unix seconds. Must be between `XOCHI_LIMIT_ORDERS_MIN_RESTING_SECONDS` (600) and `XOCHI_LIMIT_ORDERS_MAX_RESTING_SECONDS` (7d) ahead. The pull authorization is valid until exactly this.

from_amount.description: Origin amount in smallest units. The pull authorization is minted for exactly this.

limit_price.description: Floor, in `to_token` base units per ONE WHOLE `from_token`. The payout floor is `from_amount * limit_price / 10^from_decimals` and is returned as `minToAmount`.

trigger_condition.description: `gte` fills when the oracle rate (to per from) is at or above `limit_price`. `lte` is accepted by the signed struct but refused at prepare in v1 (a stop order needs a floor the struct does not carry).

eip712.description: `LimitOrder` typed data (domain `Xochi Limit Order` v1, chainId = from_chain_id, verifyingContract 0x0). Identical to what `@xochi/shared buildLimitOrderEip712Data` produces for the same terms.

minToAmount.description: The payout floor in `to_token` base units. A fill pays at least this or does not happen.

orderId.description: The order id; also the `intentId` inside the signed struct and of the fill.

pullAuthorization.description: ERC-3009 `ReceiveWithAuthorization` or Permit2 `PermitWitnessTransferFrom` typed data, valid until `expiresAt`.

lastObservedRate.description: Last oracle rate seen, `to` per `from` in whole units.

status.description: `executing` and later are driven by the fill's intent lifecycle (poll `GET /xochi/status/{orderId}` for the intent).

signature.description: Signature over `eip712` from prepare (EOA 65 bytes, or an ERC-1271 envelope).

PaymentMethod.description:
The pull mechanism of the served `pull_authorization`: on EVM routes the
label always agrees with its `primaryType` (#828). USDC public ->
`erc3009` for an EOA, `permit2` for a smart-account wallet on a chain
whose XochiPull proxy cannot execute a bytes pull yet; other ERC-20
public -> `permit2`; stealth/shielded -> `pimlico` (the recipient's
sponsored claim flow -- the payer still signs the served
`pull_authorization`). Deposit-address origins carry no
`pull_authorization`; dispatch those on `deposit_address` instead.

QuoteRequest.description:
`required` reflects the default `exact_input` direction. For
`exact_output`, send `output_amount` instead of `from_amount` (exactly one
amount is required, matched to `swap_kind`; sending both is rejected).

attestations.description: Optional ZKSAR attestations for server-side trust scoring.

deadline.description: Unix timestamp; defaults to ~30s ahead if omitted.

from_amount.description:
Input amount in base units (USDC = 6 decimals). Required for
`exact_input`; must be omitted for `exact_output`.

idempotency_key.description:
Caller-minted UUID naming ONE deposit-route allocation attempt
(#1044). Scoped to the presenting token's `kid`. The same caller
repeating the same deal under the same key receives the original
quote verbatim and allocates nothing, for as long as that route
still accepts deposits.

The deal a key names is exactly these fields, `0x` hex values
(addresses and stealth pubkeys alike) case-folded and a defaulted
`recipient_address` resolved to
`wallet`: `wallet`, `from_chain_id`, `to_chain_id`, `from_token`,
`to_token`, `swap_kind`, `from_amount`, `output_amount`,
`recipient_address`, `refund_address`, `settlement_preference`,
`slippage_bps`, `stealth_spending_pub_key`,
`stealth_viewing_pub_key`, `origin`. `deadline`, `trust_score`,
`attestations` and `preview` are NOT part of it, so a retry that
recomputes its deadline or re-fetches its attestations still
replays.

Outcomes: a different deal under the same key answers
`422 idempotency_key_reused`; a route that no longer accepts
deposits -- its deadline passed, its intent terminal, or the quote
it was priced from gone (that one does not survive a deploy
cutover) -- answers `422 idempotency_key_expired`; a concurrent
duplicate answers `409 idempotency_key_in_flight` with
`Retry-After`; an unreadable store, or an instance (or caller share)
already at its keyed-allocation limit, answers
`503 idempotency_unavailable` with `Retry-After`. Ignored on
non-deposit (EVM) origins, which allocate nothing at quote time and
are re-priced on every call.

preview.description:
Price the route without allocating anything: no quote record, no
intent, no origin-pull authorization, no deposit address. The
response carries neither `eip712` nor `deposit_address` and cannot
be executed. Use it for indicative pricing before an explicit
allocation under `idempotency_key`.

recipient_address.description:
Optional. Destination payout address, validated against
`to_chain_id`. Defaults to `wallet`, which is correct whenever
`wallet` is already a destination-VM address (EVM -> EVM, or a
Tron-origin route quoted from an EVM wallet).

Send it explicitly when it is not: an EVM -> Tron route needs the
base58 payout address, and a Tron-origin route quoted from a base58
wallet needs the EVM one. Omitting it there is rejected rather than
defaulted, so a fill can never pay a wrong-VM address. Echoed on the
response and bound into the signed `eip712` intent.

refund_address.description:
Optional. Origin-chain refund target, validated against
`from_chain_id` (a refund executes on the origin chain). Not
defaulted: a self-custody deposit refunds safely to its on-chain
sender. Send it when the origin sender is not the user -- an exchange
withdrawal address cannot receive an unexpected inbound refund -- and
it takes precedence over the sender fallback.

swap_kind.description:
Quote direction. `exact_input`: `from_amount` is the input and the
solver returns the computed `to_amount`. `exact_output`:
`output_amount` is the exact destination amount and the solver
back-computes the required `from_amount` (returned in the response),
reflecting the same fee and gas floor as the input path.

trust_score.description:
Optional. Higher scores unlock cheaper trading fees and the
stealth/shielded settlement options. See
[trust tier table](xochi.md#fee-tiers).

wallet.description:
The user's account address. On an EVM origin it is the account the
origin pull debits and the key that signs `eip712`, so it must be a
valid address on `from_chain_id`.

A deposit-address origin (Tron) debits nothing -- the user funds a
per-intent `deposit_address` -- so either form is accepted there: the
origin-chain (base58) sending address, or the EVM account address of
a client that holds one EVM wallet. Send `recipient_address` for the
payout and `refund_address` for an origin-chain refund target rather
than overloading this field.

claim_info.description: Present when the route is a stealth settlement.

deposit_address.description:
Solver's receive address on the origin chain for non-EVM routes
(TVM/SVM). The user sends `from_amount` of `from_token` directly to
this address; a deposit watcher triggers settlement. Mutually
exclusive with `pull_authorization`: exactly one is present per
quote (or neither, if the chain is not yet supported).

deposit_attestation.description:
Present on deposit-address routes: a `0x` + 65-byte secp256k1
EIP-191 `personal_sign` signature over the quote's binding fields.
The client MUST verify it recovers to
`capabilities.deposit_attestation_signer` before sending funds to
`deposit_address`, and fail closed otherwise. Null only when the
signer key is unconfigured.

The signed message is 17 `\n`-joined lines opening with the version
tag `xochi-deposit-attestation:v2`, in order: intent_id, quote_id,
wallet, from_chain_id, from_token, from_amount, deposit_address,
deposit_deadline, to_chain_id, to_token, to_amount, min_to_amount,
recipient, stealth_spending_pub_key, stealth_viewing_pub_key,
settlement_preference.

v1 signed only the six origin-side fields, which proved the venue
issued this address for this intent but nothing about whose intent
it was -- an attacker holding the channel could substitute an
entire valid quote of their own and every client check passed. v2
signs the destination side too, so a substituted quote has to be
economically identical to the one requested.

Encoding: a `0x`-prefixed value is lowercased (case-sensitive
prefix check); everything else is verbatim, because base58 Tron
addresses are case-sensitive and folding one yields a different,
still-plausible address. Absent optional values
(`deposit_deadline`, either stealth key) are an EMPTY line, never
omitted and never `null` -- the line count is fixed at 17. See
docs/api/xochi.md for the full spec.

deposit_deadline.description:
Present on deposit-address routes: unix seconds until which a landed
deposit is still filled (rather than refunded). Decoupled from
`expires_at` (the quote TTL) because a manual TRC-20 withdrawal
routinely takes longer than the TTL. Use it for a client countdown.

eip712.description:
Full EIP-712 typed data: `domain`, `types`, `primaryType`,
`message`. Pass directly to `eth_signTypedData_v4`. The
`domain.version` reflects `XOCHI_EIP712_VERSION` (e.g. `1-prod`)
and `domain.salt` = keccak256(version) binds the signature to the
deployment. The signed `message` has no `nonce` field -- replay is
guarded by `intent_id`.

estimated_gas_cost.description:
Destination gas estimate in the destination chain's **native** gas-token
wei (string) -- POL wei on Polygon, BNB wei on BNB Chain, ETH wei on
Ethereum and its rollups. The native symbol is that of `to_chain_id`;
do NOT assume ETH (a Polygon quote returns POL wei, ~13000x cheaper than
ETH). This value is execution-only; the rollup L1 data-posting cost is
reflected only in `estimated_gas_cost_usd`, so render fiat from that USD
field rather than converting this wei value. A successful quote always
carries a live estimate; if the gas/price oracle is down the quote is
rejected (503), not zeroed.

estimated_gas_cost_usd.description:
Destination gas estimate in USD. This is the authoritative field for
fiat display: unlike `estimated_gas_cost` it includes the rollup L1
data-posting cost, and it is priced in the destination chain's native
gas token (e.g. POL for Polygon), so it is correct on every chain.

fee_breakdown.description:
Optional itemized fee anatomy (economics.md Part 1). Present only when
the layered fee model is active (`:xochi_layered_fees`). The frontend
renders the per-layer split; `fee` stays the back-compat summary.

pull_authorization.description:
EIP-712 typed data authorizing Riddler to pull `from_amount` of
`from_token` from the user on the origin chain: ERC-3009
`ReceiveWithAuthorization` for USDC, otherwise Permit2
`PermitWitnessTransferFrom`. Same shape as `eip712`
(`domain`/`types`/`primaryType`/`message`). The client MUST sign it
with `eth_signTypedData_v4` and return the signature as
`pull_signature` on /execute. Riddler collects origin funds before
settling the destination, so /execute fails closed without it.
Mutually exclusive with `deposit_address`.

recipient_address.description:
Destination payout address, validated against `to_chain_id` (EVM
0x-hex, TVM/SVM base58). Echoes the request's `recipient_address`,
defaulting to `wallet` for same-VM routes. For a cross-VM route it is
the destination-chain address the fill pays, distinct from the
origin-side `wallet`. Also bound into the signed `eip712` intent.

settlement_options.description:
One entry per settlement type with its per-quote availability. The
client reads `available` (not membership) to gate each option.

expected_fill_seconds.description: Conservative upper bound used by clients to size poll timeouts.

SettlementOption.description:
A settlement type with its per-quote availability. The client reads
`available` to enable/disable each option (e.g. the stealth toggle) and
shows `reason` when it is off, instead of inferring from a bare type list.

available.description:
Whether this settlement type is offered for this quote (the trust/
attestation tier permits it AND the deploy allow-list enables it).

reason.description:
Present only when `available` is false: a short human-readable reason
(e.g. "requires a higher trust tier", "not offered by this solver").

SettlementType.description:
`public` = standard ERC-3009/Permit2 transfer to wallet.
`stealth` = ERC-5564 + ERC-4337 counterfactual SimpleAccount.
`shielded` = Aztec L2 shielded note (returns `aztec_unavailable`
until the sidecar is deployed -- see HANDOVER.md
XOCHI-SETTLE-AZTEC).

addresses.description: Chain ID (as string) to token address.

gasless_origin.description: True when the origin pull needs no prior approval (ERC-3009). Permit2 tokens require a one-time approve of the Permit2 contract. Always false for deposit_address flows.

pull_method.description:
How origin funds are collected for this token. `erc3009` and `permit2`
are gasless EVM flows. `deposit_address` is used for non-EVM chains
(Tron, Solana) where the user deposits directly to the solver's address.

WalletSignature.description:
Wallet signature, hex-encoded. An EOA sends 65 bytes (r||s||v). A smart
account (ERC-4337, EIP-7702, Safe) sends its ERC-1271 envelope, which is
longer and wallet-specific -- do not assume 65 bytes. Verified by
`ecrecover` when it is 65 bytes and recovers to the quote's `wallet`,
otherwise by calling ERC-1271 `isValidSignature` on that wallet.
Counterfactual (undeployed) accounts are not supported: ERC-6492
wrappers are not unwrapped.

bearerAuth.description:
Per-caller token. The token's `kid` is tagged on every auth
telemetry event for attribution. Configure via
`XOCHI_API_TOKENS_JSON`.

info.description:
Customer-facing API for Riddler's Xochi launch surface. Riddler is the
solver backend for the Xochi protocol (ETH's Friendly Dark Pool); this
spec describes the HTTP surface Riddler itself serves under `/xochi/*`.

Source of truth: the Plug router at
`lib/riddler/integrations/xochi/router.ex` and the schemas under
`lib/riddler/integrations/xochi/schemas/`. CI runs
`test/riddler/integrations/xochi/openapi_riddler_contract_test.exs` to
flag drift.

See also:
  - `docs/api/xochi.md` -- prose API guide with examples
  - `docs/architecture/decisions/0005-xochi-integration.md` -- design rationale
  - `HANDOVER.md` -- cross-repo context (Riddler / Xochi / raxol_payments)
info.title: Riddler Xochi API

get.description: Machine-readable token x chain x direction matrix, plus the cross-chain rule, USD order bounds, and per-token origin pull method. Lets clients drive their token selector from the solver instead of a hand-maintained config. Public discovery endpoint; no authentication required.
Public discovery endpoint; no authentication required.

post.description:
Gasless ERC-4337 claim where Riddler derives the stealth key from
keys supplied by the caller, sponsors the UserOp via Pimlico, and
submits.

**This endpoint is OFF in production** (`XOCHI_ALLOW_SERVER_SIGN=false`)
because the recipient's private keys travel in the request body and
through Riddler memory. Public callers must use the two-step
client-signed flow:
  1. `POST /xochi/claim/prepare`
  2. `POST /xochi/claim/submit`

Returns 410 `server_sign_disabled` while disabled.

Required scope: `claim`.

example.message: Server-side claim is disabled. Use POST /xochi/claim/prepare + POST /xochi/claim/submit (client-signed).

post.description:
The client supplies the counterfactual address it scanned from the
ERC-5564 announcement; the server resolves the intent from it. Returns
the unsigned UserOperation hash for the client to sign with the
stealth-derived private key. The hash is held server-side under the
userOpHash for 5 minutes; submit via `/xochi/claim/submit` within that
window.

**Proof of control** (#993): the response discloses the intent binding
and sponsors paymaster gas, so the request should carry a stealth-key
signature proving control of the counterfactual -- the same key that
must sign the UserOp at submit. Sign `keccak256` of the UTF-8 string

    xochi-claim-prepare-v1:{chain_id}:{counterfactual}:{recipient}:{issued_at}

(base-10 integers, 0x-prefixed lowercase addresses; `chain_id` is the
CLAIM chain -- the intent's destination, the same `chainId` echoed in
the ClaimPrepareResponse; `issued_at` unix seconds, accepted from 300s
in the past to 120s in the future of server time) raw with the stealth
key -- the same primitive as the UserOp-hash signature, no EIP-191
prefix -- and send it as `ownership_proof` with `proof_issued_at`.
Published conformance vectors for the challenge:
`GET /xochi/vectors/claim-prepare-proof.json`.

A proof is valid for ONE prepare: a verified signature is recorded and
a repeat is refused -- re-sign with a fresh `issued_at` to retry.

A present proof is always verified. While the deploy runs
`XOCHI_CLAIM_PROOF_REQUIRED=false`, an absent proof is tolerated, a
wrong-signer/undecodable/replayed one answers 403
`ownership_proof_invalid`, and a stale one 400 `ownership_proof_stale`.
Once the flag is on, a request without a valid proof (absent, wrong
signer, or replayed) answers a 404 identical to an unknown
counterfactual -- the response never confirms which counterfactuals
hold live unclaimed payments; server telemetry still records the true
reason. `ownership_proof_stale` (400) survives in both modes: signer
recovery runs before the freshness check, so only the key holder can
ever see it.

Required scope: `claim_prepare`.

schema.description:
One counterfactual (`counterfactual_address`) or several (`counterfactual_addresses`, #1116). The multi form is the "claim all" a stealth recipient with N payments needs: N accounts by construction, one request, one op per account. Sending both keys is a 422 -- they are different requests, and guessing which was meant would put every named account's sponsorship behind the guess.
The multi form REQUIRES an ownership proof per account whatever `XOCHI_CLAIM_PROOF_REQUIRED` says: the rollout posture exists for the deployed single-account frontend, and a 20-wide proofless refusal array would classify scanned announcements. It is also charged one rate-limiter slot per account, and its fan-out shares a budget of `XOCHI_CLAIM_FAN_OUT_BUDGET_MS` (8 seconds by default) sized under the 15-second client timeout: accounts the budget does not reach are refused transiently per entry (`reason: fan_out_deadline`, nothing spent on them) and a wallet with more claimable accounts than one request serves retries the remainder. An account the budget ran out DURING is refused `reason: fan_out_overran` with a `retryAfter` sized to outlast the work still running for it (it withdraws what it prepared when it finishes); retrying it sooner answers the unknown-counterfactual 404, because its proof digest is still held.

200.description: Prepared claim, or one prepared op per named account

example.message: Ownership proof timestamp outside the freshness window; re-sign against server_time and retry

400.description: Ownership proof timestamp outside the freshness window

example.message: Multi-account claim is momentarily unavailable; retry

503.description: Transient (#853) -- honour `Retry-After`. A dependency of the prepare is unavailable (the counterfactual recompute, the account probe, the op builder, the paymaster, or the prepared-op store; `details.reason` names it), or, for the multi form, the fan-out could not be started or collected, or every account was refused and at least one refusal was transient (the first transient one is answered). Nothing from this request was delivered: an account the multi form had already prepared is withdrawn -- its op deleted and its proof released, its rate-limiter slot still spent -- so the same body can be retried.

post.description:
Rebuilds the claim record for an announced counterfactual the solver's
store no longer has, so `/xochi/claim/prepare` can resolve it again.
Records announced before the store became durable did not survive a
blue/green cutover; the funds are still at their counterfactual, but the
map from counterfactual to stealth owner was lost.

The client supplies the stealth owner EOA it derived with its viewing
key -- the one field not derivable from public data, and the reason a
server-side reconciler cannot do this. It is verified, not trusted: the
offered owner must reproduce the announced counterfactual under CREATE2,
and the announcement must be one this solver made, read from the
transaction receipt named by `announcement_tx_hash`.

The payout terms (`to_token`, `to_amount`) are read from the
announcement's own on-chain metadata and can never be supplied by the
caller -- there is no request field for them.

Idempotent: a call for a counterfactual that already has a claimable
record returns `rebuilt: false` and writes nothing.

Required scope: `claim_rebuild`.

example.message: The offered owner address does not derive the announced counterfactual

422.description: Permanent refusal -- the offered owner does not derive the counterfactual (`owner_mismatch`), the transaction holds no announcement from this solver (`announcement_not_found`), its metadata is unreadable (`announcement_undecodable`), it names a foreign account factory (`factory_mismatch`), it announces the counterfactual from an announcer/solver this deploy is not configured with (`announcer_mismatch`, i.e. a key rotation since the announcement), or announcing is not configured for that chain (`announcer_not_configured`). Retrying the same body cannot clear any of these.

example.message: Could not read the announcement transaction receipt; retry shortly

503.description: Transient -- the announcement receipt could not be read (`announcement_unreadable`) or the counterfactual could not be computed. Retry shortly.

post.summary: Restore a lost stealth claim record

post.description:
Submits the client-signed UserOperation to the Pimlico bundler.
Requires a prepare call within the last 5 minutes for the same
userOpHash.

The multi form (`signatures`, #1116) submits each op independently --
there is no batching at the bundler -- and all three arrays it returns
are keyed by `userOpHash`. At most 20 entries, and the whole fan-out
shares a budget of `XOCHI_CLAIM_FAN_OUT_BUDGET_MS` (8 seconds by
default) sized under the 15-second client timeout. An entry the
budget did not reach broadcast nothing and answers 503
`service_unavailable` with `reason: fan_out_deadline`; its signature
is still good, so resend just that entry.

The single form waits for the receipt at most 10 seconds by default
(`XOCHI_CLAIM_SUBMIT_RECEIPT_WAIT_MS` on the deploy), so it answers
inside a 15-second client timeout; each multi-form entry waits the
smaller of that and what is left of the fan-out budget when it
starts. The op is recorded as broadcast the moment the bundler
accepts it, BEFORE that wait, so a request abandoned mid-wait -- a
client timeout, a disconnect -- still leaves a retry that polls it.

An op the bundler ACCEPTED whose receipt was not seen inside the wait
is not a failure: the single form answers 503 with
`reason: receipt_pending` and the op hash, the multi form lists it in
`pending`. It is in the mempool and will execute. Submitting the same
`userOpHash` again POLLS that op -- it is never resent -- and answers
200 once its receipt is seen, which is also when the claim is recorded.
An op the bundler refused was not broadcast: a verdict about the op
(bad signature, simulation revert) is a 422, a bundler outage a 503.

Sending `user_op_hash` and `signatures` together is a 422: they are
different requests and neither is safe to guess.

Required scope: `claim_submit`.

200.description: Claim submitted, or one result per signature

example.message: No prepared claim found -- call POST /claim/prepare first
Prepared claim expired (5-minute window) -- call POST /claim/prepare again

410.description: Prepared claim expired (5-minute window, from the broadcast for an op the bundler accepted), or the op was mined and REVERTED: its nonce is spent and nothing moved. Either way, prepare again.

example.message: Claim op accepted by the bundler and not yet mined; retry the same submit to poll it (it is not resent)

503.description: Transient (#853) -- honour `Retry-After`. The op was accepted by the bundler and not yet mined inside the bounded receipt wait (`reason: receipt_pending`, with `details.op_hash`: resubmit the same `userOpHash` to poll it; it is not resent), or the bundler was unavailable and nothing was broadcast (`bundler_unavailable`). The multi form never answers this for its budget alone: its first entry always starts, so a budget refusal is a per-entry `fan_out_deadline` inside the 200 body.

post.description:
Returns a quote keyed by `quote_id` and `intent_id` with tier-based
fees (0.10-0.30% trading + privacy premium) and the full EIP-712
typed data the user signs. Quotes are valid for ~30s (configurable).

Required scope: `quote`.

**Deposit-address origins allocate.** A Tron-origin quote binds a
per-intent deposit address, an intent record and a signed attestation
to one `intent_id`, so a retry after a timeout or a lost 2xx would
mint a second route while the first still accepts funds. Send
`idempotency_key` (a caller-minted UUID, one per allocation attempt)
to make such a retry safe: the same authenticated caller repeating the
same deal under the same key receives the ORIGINAL quote (same
`intent_id`, `quote_id`, `deposit_address`, `deposit_attestation`,
`deposit_deadline`) and allocates nothing, for as long as that route
still accepts deposits. It binds only deposit-address routes; an EVM
quote allocates nothing and is re-priced on every call, key or not.
`preview: true` prices a route without allocating anything at all.

422.description:
Validation failed (`validation_failed`, with the offending fields
in `details`), the route was declined for a documented reason
(see `ErrorCode`), or the `idempotency_key` cannot be honoured:
it already names a deposit-route quote with different inputs
(`idempotency_key_reused`), or the route it named no longer
accepts deposits (`idempotency_key_expired`). Both are permanent
for this request: a key names one deal, so send a new key.

503.description:
Transient: the gas/ETH-price/L1-blob oracle is down, so the gas floor
can't be priced (`gas_price_unavailable`), the origin token price feed
is cold (`price_unavailable`), no solver is available on the origin
chain (`origin_unavailable`), or a deposit-address origin cannot
allocate right now (`origin_unavailable`). Retry after a short backoff.

An origin that is **switched off** on this deployment is not a 503 --
it answers `422 origin_not_enabled`, because no amount of retrying
will clear it. Retry `origin_unavailable`; do not retry
`origin_not_enabled`.

Destination inventory shortfalls come in two shapes.
`insufficient_liquidity` means the float is short and nothing is
being done about it right now -- retry on your own backoff, or try a
smaller amount. `pre_positioning` means the same shortfall with a
top-up already dispatched, so `Retry-After` and `details.retry_after`
carry the move's estimated seconds. Nothing is reserved for the
quote either way: the top-up restores the shared float, and whoever
quotes next gets it.

A keyed deposit-route quote whose replay record, lock backend or
stored quote cannot be read answers `idempotency_unavailable` with
`Retry-After`, and so does one that arrives while the instance -- or
the caller's share of it -- is already running its full complement of
keyed allocations, or one whose previous attempt was interrupted
between its two writes. Nothing was allocated; the same key retried
replays or allocates exactly once. An unreadable store is never
reported as an expired route: that answer is permanent, and its
remedy would allocate a second route.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. Present on `pre_positioning` (the dispatched top-up's estimated landing) and on `idempotency_unavailable`.

post.description:
Server-to-server callback used by the Xochi worker to ask Riddler
to execute a settlement (stealth `DirectTransfer` or shielded
Aztec note). Most customers do NOT call this directly -- it is
exposed for documentation completeness and Xochi-backend
integrators.

Only the caller whose token (`kid`) requested the quote can settle
the intent: a foreign intent answers the same 404 as a nonexistent
id, by design, and the refusal lands before the already-settled fast
path so the settlement tx hash is never disclosed. Intents predating
ownership stamping and intents created under the legacy shared token
stay settleable by any `settle`-scoped caller.

Required scope: `settle`.

example.message: A settlement for this intent is already in progress -- retry shortly or poll GET /xochi/status/:intent_id

409.description: A settlement for this intent is already in progress

post.summary: Settlement callback from the Xochi backend

get.description:
Returns the current state of an intent. Lifecycle is
`pending -> executing -> bridging -> settling -> completed`, with
terminal states `completed | refunded | failed | expired`. Deposit
refunds report non-terminal `refund_pending` after the owed-refund
ledger is written, and advance to terminal `refunded` only once a real
refund transaction hash is recorded. When `/execute` runs asynchronously
(202), the origin-pull intent rests at the non-terminal `pull_pending`
state until its receipt confirms.

Only the caller whose token (`kid`) requested the quote can read the
intent: a foreign intent answers the same 404 as a nonexistent id, by
design. Intents predating ownership stamping and intents created under
the legacy shared token stay readable by any `status`-scoped caller.

Required scope: `status`.

What `POST /xochi/claim/prepare` will build for `action: call` on this deploy (#1115): per chain, the permitted `{target, selector}` pairs with their argument policies, sponsored-gas ceiling and whether a successful submit ends the intent. Served rather than hand-copied because a copied allowlist diverges by ADMITTING what the server refuses, and nothing notices until a refusal reaches a user mid-claim. Reflects the deploy's `XOCHI_CLAIM_CALL_ALLOWLIST_JSON`, so it is the live answer and not a compile-time snapshot. Public; ETag-validated.

policy.description: `{type: address, oneOf: [...]}`, `{type: address, mustEqual: ...}` or `{type: uint256, max: intent.toAmount}`.

target.description: A 0x address, or the marker `intent.toToken` for a row scoped to the claimed intent's own token.

terminal.description: Whether a successful submit marks the intent completed.

304.description: Not modified; If-None-Match matched the current ETag

get.description: The byte-exact conformance vectors for the `/xochi/claim/prepare` ownership-proof challenge (#993). Riddler is authoritative for this set -- it VERIFIES the proof, so the encoding it accepts is the contract, and a frontend signer tested only against its own challenge encoding passes for any string, including one this server refuses. Each vector carries the inputs, the exact challenge string, its keccak256 digest, a well-known test private key, the r||s||v signature, and the signer address. Public discovery endpoint; no authentication required; ETag-validated. Send `If-None-Match` and poll on a schedule, not per request.

get.description: The byte-exact conformance vectors for the deposit attestation, as produced by this server. Riddler is authoritative for this set -- it signs and the client only verifies -- so a client MUST NOT recompute the expectations locally: a verifier checked against its own output passes for any encoding, including a wrong one. Diff this against your copy in CI, or compare `version` against `deposit_attestation_version` on `/xochi/capabilities`. Public discovery endpoint; no authentication required; ETag-validated. Rate limited like any other read: send `If-None-Match` and poll on a schedule, not per request.
